title: Extended Cr Bound with Diversity Injection
scientific_hypothesis: The optimal Cr absorbing layer thickness exceeds the previous 4.0 nm upper bound; extending to 6.0 nm while injecting diversity in bottom 30% of candidates will discover higher-performing interference pathways without losing proven baseline configurations.
design_principle: Preserve the verified 20-layer Cr/HfO2/SiO2/Al topology from iteration_24 best candidate while widening Cr thickness search space and introducing deterministic diversity to escape local optima.
proposed_topology: Air | Cr (layer 0) | HfO2 (layer 1) | SiO2 (layer 2) | HfO2 (layer 3) | SiO2 (layer 4) | HfO2 (layer 5) | SiO2 (layer 6) | HfO2 (layer 7) | SiO2 (layer 8) | HfO2 (layer 9) | SiO2 (layer 10) | HfO2 (layer 11) | SiO2 (layer 12) | HfO2 (layer 13) | SiO2 (layer 14) | HfO2 (layer 15) | SiO2 (layer 16) | HfO2 (layer 17) | SiO2 (layer 18) | HfO2 (layer 19) | Al substrate. Total 20 finite layers.
manufacturing_considerations: Cr thickness up to 6.0 nm remains fabricable via sputtering
theory_basis: Admittance locus method for metal-dielectric multilayer optimization
D/M/D interference design principle for spectral selectivity
expected_advantages: Wider Cr search space captures optimal absorbing thickness
known_risks: Cr thickness >4 nm may reduce visible absorptance if too thick
Diversity may temporarily reduce best_target_score during exploration
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar stack on Al substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: Cr | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2. Initialize from iteration_24 best candidate thicknesses [1.0, 123.0, 94.0, 4.0, 22.0, 52.0, 139.0, 83.0, 40.0, 98.0, 231.0, 43.0, 4.0, 123.0, 48.0, 113.0, 155.0, 14.0, 70.0, 154.0] nm. Set Cr layer (index 0) thickness bounds to [0.5, 6.0] nm. Set all dielectric layers (indices 1-19) bounds to [1.0, 300.0] nm. Use gradient_thickness optimizer. Initialize 70% of candidates from baseline with small perturbations; initialize remaining 30% with random thickness draws uniformly distributed in [baseline - 50 nm, baseline + 50 nm] for each layer. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized. Spectral objectives: maximize absorptance in 400-700 nm band, maximize reflectance in 700-2000 nm band. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 400-700 nm, 700-2000 nm. soft objectives: high absorptance in 400-700 nm; low reflectance in 400-700 nm; high reflectance in 700-2000 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflectance in 400-700 nm; high absorptance in 700-2000 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 20.
revision_reason: Extended Cr upper bound from 4.0 nm to 6.0 nm per feedback directive; added deterministic diversity protocol (30% random reinitialization) to inject novel interference pathways while preserving proven baselines.
